And it is still an oddity today in the world where most people are right-handed. And so, binya means the son of my right hand is still the dominant hand, but that was to the south. Because evil always comes from the north or the left hand. Have you never heard the saying that just came out of nowhere, that came out of left field? That's the idea of surprise. explicit_propositions.text: This is podcast number 24.
The primary directions in the Bible are east and west, not north and south.
The poles were not discovered during biblical times.
Jerusalem sits on a ridge known today as the Western Ridge or Patriarchal Highway.
In ancient times, people stood on the Mount of Olives and faced east toward the rising sun.
The Hebrew word 'cadem' translates to 'east' but literally means 'forward'.
When facing east, behind the person is west, to the right is south, and to the left is north.
Ancient orientation relied on facing the sunrise; east defined the front, west the back.
The term 'orientation' derives from facing east, not determining true north.
In biblical tradition, the right hand symbolizes strength and dominance.

assumptions.text: A person’s spatial orientation is fundamentally tied to cultural and religious symbolic systems.
Directional meaning in ancient texts reflects lived experience and physical posture.
The Hebrew language encodes spatial relationships through action-oriented terms like 'forward'.
Cultural continuity exists between ancient Near Eastern practices and modern linguistic remnants.
Right-handedness is culturally normative and associated with power and virtue.
Left-hand symbolism is inherently linked to negativity or deviation in biblical worldview.
Geographical orientation based on solar movement was practical and widespread in pre-modern societies.
Modern political movements may draw symbolic inspiration from ancient directional metaphors.
Listeners are familiar with basic geography and biblical references to interpret the explanation.
Audience members value historical context for understanding scriptural language.
